2607.24155.title: Looking for Affect in Spontaneous Finnish Speech through Linguistic Interpretability
2607.24155.paper_summary: Existing research on affect in speech has shown how acoustic surface characteristics and content-related linguistic aspects of speech both relate to perceived emotional arousal and valence. However, it is not clear what the relative contributions of these two factors are in the perceptual process. This is especially true for Finnish, for which most existing studies focus on either acoustic-phonetic or text analysis. This paper presents a study where we systematically explore the combinatory role of text- and audio-based features in modeling the human perception of valence and arousal using a newly released affective speech corpus for spontaneous Finnish. We show that the combination of text- and audio-based features improves valence regression results over the individual modalities, whereas for arousal regression the complementary effect is not substantial. The results support prior findings from other languages, providing new data and knowledge on spontaneous Finnish speech.
2607.24155.paper_summary_zh: 現有的語音情感研究顯示，聲學表面特徵和與內容相關的語言方面均與感知的情感喚起和價值相關。然而，這兩個因素在感知過程中的相對貢獻尚不清楚。這對於芬蘭語尤其如此，因為現有的大多數研究專注於聲學-語音或文本分析。本文呈現了一項研究，我們系統地探討文本和音頻特徵在建模人類對價值和喚起的感知中的組合作用，使用了一個新發布的自發芬蘭語情感語音語料庫。我們顯示，文本和音頻特徵的組合在價值回歸結果上優於單一模態，而在喚起回歸中，互補效應並不顯著。這些結果支持了其他語言的先前發現，為自發芬蘭語語音提供了新的數據和知識。
